hero.headline: Indian River County approves expansion of Westside Racquet Club in Vero Beach
hero.body:
The Indian River County Commission approved a special exception use and Phase 1 site plan on August 4 for the renovation and expansion of the Westside Racquet Club, a 1970s-era facility in Vero Beach that has fallen into disrepair in recent years. The 6.89-acre property is located east of 43rd Avenue Southwest, north of 6th Lane Southwest and south of Fifth Place Southwest.

Phase 1 of the project will restore the existing eight tennis courts, construct four new padel courts and construct associated site improvements including utilities, stormwater, parking and landscaping. The existing 2,400-square-foot clubhouse will be restored in Phase 2, which will also add two padel courts. Phase 3 will include a pool house and four pickleball courts, while Phase 4 will add two additional tennis courts. The Planning Zoning Commission voted unanimously to recommend approval on June 11 but added a special condition due to concerns about potential noise pollution and light infiltration onto adjacent properties.

Vice-Chairwoman Laura Moss expressed concerns about voting on the special exception use that would cover all four phases while only approving the Phase 1 site plan, saying commissioners were being asked to vote in the blind. She also raised concerns about pickleball noise and lighting impacts on neighboring residents. Planning Development Services Director John Stoll said the county can require traffic studies once the project exceeds 400 average daily trips and can implement noise mitigation measures including limiting nighttime lighting and operational hours, requiring special paddles and balls, and increasing separation from neighbors.

District 3 Commissioner Joseph Earman pointed out the continuity of use on the parcel and said he had heard from residents who think the improvements will add value to their property. Mark Jaffe, a 4th Lane Southwest resident, was the only public speaker and said he would like to see the project move forward. The County Commission voted unanimously to approve the requests.
hero.article_text: The aerial and location map for the 6.89-acre property home to the current Westside Racquet Club whose new owner had requested a conditional use permit and Phase 1 site plan approval for a significant remodeling and expansion project. The aerial and location map for the 6.89-acre property home to the current Westside Racquet Club whose new owner had requested a conditional use permit and Phase 1 site plan approval for a significant remodeling and expansion project. VERO BEACH – The Indian River County Commission approved the special exception use and Phase 1 site plan Aug. 4 for the renovation and expansion of the existing Westside Racquet Club, a 1970s-era facility that in recent years has fallen into disrepair. The Planning Zoning Commission previously heard the same requests on June 11, voting unanimously to recommend approval but adding a special condition of approval due to concerns about potential noise pollution and light infiltration onto adjacent property owners. Senior Planner Kelly McKinley introduced the agenda item during the latest meeting. “Before you today is the Westside Racquet Club’s special exception use and site plan approval request to expand the existing facility with the intent of restoring it, as well as providing additional enhancements,” she said. “The subject parcel is 6.89 acres located east of 43rd Avenue Southwest, north of 6th Lane Southwest and south of Fifth Place Southwest. The special exception use will cover all four phases, [but] only Phase 1 is before you for site plan approval at this time. The additional phases will subsequently be approved.” McKinley proceeded to provide further details on the color-coded phasing plan for the property, which currently houses a small, existing racquet court building and eight tennis courts. “The white [Phase 1] is going to restore the existing eight tennis courts, construct four new padel courts and construct associated site improvements like utilities, stormwater, parking and landscaping,” she continued. “The green will restore the existing 2,400-square-foot clubhouse and construct two additional padel courts. Phase 3, the pink, will include the pool house as a clubhouse amenity and construct four pickleball courts. Phase 4, the blue, will consist of two additional tennis courts.” McKinley also described the proposed stormwater improvements and landscaping plan, which will include a stormwater pond along the southern part of the project and a swale. Additional landscaping will include a 20-foot buffer along 43rd Avenue Southwest and a 30-foot-Type B landscape buffer around the other three perimeters. Foundation plantings will be installed around the pool and the existing clubhouse building. After she recommended approval and described the P Z Commission’s additional condition of approval, Vice-Chairwoman Laura Moss posed her first question and initial concerns to staff. “I’m just confirming what they’re adding,” she said. “So, it’s four padel courts, a pool and four pickleball courts. Is that reason why this is a special exception?” “The site is zoned RS-3,” McKinley replied. “Within that zoning district, the use itself is the special exception.” Chairman Deryl Loar chimed in with another important fact. “I think it’s also because you’re going over a threshold and you’re expanding the existing use by more than 10 percent,” he said. Vice-Chairwoman Moss then addressed the heart of her concern, the fact that all subsequent phases would be administratively approved and not require any further public hearings. “I think to vote on this, we’re in effect being asked operationally to vote in the blind because I don’t know what it’s going to be in totality,” she continued. “Once we grant the special exception, basically anything goes [and] we lose control of it. On top of that, if we change it, that land maintains the special exception designation no matter who owns it.” Vice-Chairwoman Moss acknowledged that she’d viewed the June Planning Zoning Commission hearing and lamented what she viewed as a lack of technical expertise for the concerned neighboring residents. She also bemoaned the fact the applicant’s representative was not present that day. “Pickleball is very loud, [and] somebody made a really good point,” she said of the earlier hearing. “The noise ordinance only applies when it’s a sustained level of sound. Pickleball’s not a sustained level of sound, so they really don’t have protection in terms of the noise. It was mentioned that the lighting would end up in peoples’ backyards. A privacy fence was suggested. I’m not comfortable that this was thoroughly addressed and will not adversely affect the public interest.” While Chairman Loar responded by insisting her comment about losing control was “not an exact description of our professional staff,” Deputy County Attorney Susan Prado provided a legal opinion of the exact task before commissioners that morning. She also attempted to alleviate some of the vice-chairwoman’s concerns about the lack of technical expertise during the P Z Commission hearing. “As was stated, none of the other phases will come back,” Prado said. “If you’re wanting to place conditions on the other phases, that will need to be placed today as well as for all phases. As far as evidence presented, affected persons can come forward and present their evidence as to issues. If there is that [pickleball noise] concern, there is case law that says both sides have to bring their own professionals and that will also include the people impacted.” For his part, District 3 Commissioner Joseph Earman pointed out the continuity of use on the parcel and local community support for the planned improvements. “Commissioners understand this has always been what it’s always been – it’s nothing different,” he said. “It just went silent because it had no ownership. I’ve heard from a few of the residents out there that think it’s great because it’ll add value to their property and everything as a whole because it is run down right now.” Vice-Chairwoman Moss’ final concern was related to potential traffic impacts, which were addressed by Planning Development Services Director John Stoll, who also touched on her noise and lighting concerns. “The traffic studies will be cumulative,” he explained. “As soon as they have a use that kicks them over the 400 average daily trips, we’ll require a traffic study. We have a number of noise-mitigation measures that we’ve found, including a new noise study specifically to pickleball. We can limit nighttime lighting and operational hours, require special paddles and balls and increase the separation from the neighbors if we need to.” There was only public speaker that evening, 4th Lane Southwest resident Mark Jaffe. “I travel on 5th Street Southwest every single day since 1996 and pass this neighborhood many times a day,” he said. “When I moved here, Westside Neighborhood was there. I drive past that dilapidated racquet club almost every single day. I would like to see this move forward.” The County Commission then voted unanimously to approve the requests. hero.headline: American Paint Horse stolen from Port St. Lucie pasture, sheriff's office seeks public help
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is asking the public for help locating a missing American Paint Horse believed to have been stolen from its owner's pasture in Port St. Lucie. The 2-year-old stallion named Strait from Above was last seen at approximately 3 p.m. Sunday at 2801 Williams Road near St. Lucie West and west of Interstate 95 in a rural area.

The horse has distinctive features including a white forelock and mane with a black and white tail, and a pinto coat with distinctive black and white spots. The breed typically stands 56 to 64 inches and weighs between 950 and 1,200 pounds, according to the American Paint Horse Association.

The sheriff's office posted on Facebook Saturday that every detail could help bring Strait from Above home safely. Authorities are asking residents, property owners, horse enthusiasts, agricultural communities, and anyone who may have seen or been offered a horse matching this description to take a close look at the identifying information.

Anyone with information can report potential sightings or tips to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office at 772-462-7300 or submit a tip by email at PatrolTips@stluciesheriff.com.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie man arrested on animal cruelty charge after video shows dog abuse
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police arrested Ricky Lee Shieferstein, 68, on Aug. 6 following an investigation into a social media video that shows a man abusing a small dog. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office received numerous reports from community members who shared the video and tagged the agency across its social media platforms. The video shows a man walking behind a dog at a concrete pool and yelling out, out, out in the grass several times and kicking the dog in its right hip at least once.

The information was turned over to the sheriff's office criminal investigations division. Detective Dawn Dale developed probable cause through her investigation and obtained an arrest warrant to charge Shieferstein with animal cruelty.

Shieferstein is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $7,500 bond. The video circulated widely on social media, sparking outrage and prompting the investigation.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office posted the case to its Facebook page with a viewer discretion warning. The agency reminded residents that the fastest and most effective way to report a crime in progress or suspicious activity is by calling 911, stating that while it actively monitors social media platforms, they are not monitored continuously and should never be relied upon to report emergencies or crimes requiring an immediate law enforcement response.

cards.headline: Road rage ends in four-vehicle crash on U.S. 1 in Port St. Lucie, man arrested
cards.teaser: A road rage confrontation between a motorcyclist and a pickup truck driver erupted into a violent four-vehicle crash on U.S. 1 Wednesday, leaving four people injured.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police responded around 6:45 p.m. Wednesday to the intersection of South U.S. Highway 1 and SE Lyngate Drive/SE Tiffany Avenue, where a red Harley-Davidson motorcycle and a black Ford Super Duty pickup truck were involved in an ongoing road rage incident. The pickup, driven by 54-year-old Kevin Lonergan, was pursuing the motorcycle as both vehicles traveled northbound on U.S. 1 and approached the intersection, according to witness statements and dash-camera video.

The motorcycle entered the intersection against a red light and collided with a black Chevrolet Silverado, throwing the 31-year-old rider from the bike. Lonergan then entered the intersection against the red signal, struck the ejected motorcyclist, and crashed head-on into a blue Toyota RAV4. The motorcyclist and two people inside the RAV4 were taken to Lawnwood Medical Center. The Silverado driver was transported to St. Lucie Medical Center.

The motorcyclist suffered serious injuries, including a brain bleed and facial fractures, and lost consciousness after the crash. He remains hospitalized in stable condition. Police arrested Lonergan for two counts of reckless driving causing serious bodily injury and one count of reckless driving causing injury. After being medically cleared, Lonergan was booked into the St. Lucie County Jail. The intersection remained closed for hours while investigators processed the scene before all lanes reopened around 2 a.m.

"These two vehicles were involved in an active road rage incident just prior to the crash, and this is based off the dash camera and witness statements that we've collected," said Officer Brittany McNally with the Port St. Detectives say the pickup, driven by 54-year-old Kevin Lonergan, was pursuing the motorcycle as both vehicles traveled northbound on U.S. 1 and approached the intersection. He remains hospitalized in stable condition.\ Based on witness statements, dash-camera video and the investigation, police arrested Lonergan for two counts of reckless driving causing serious bodily injury and one count of reckless driving causing injury. The investigative findings indicate that the pickup truck was actively pursuing that motorcyclist just moments prior to that crash, said McNally. After being medically cleared, Lonergan was booked into the St. The intersection remained closed for hours while investigators processed the scene before all lanes reopened around 2 a.m. This case does, though, serve as hopefully a powerful reminder that allowing your anger to dictate your actions behind the wheel can put multiple innocent lives at risk, McNally said.

hero.headline: Indian River County schools open Monday with some bus pickups before sunrise
hero.body:
Public schools in Indian River County open Monday, Aug. 10, for the 2026-2027 school year, with high schools starting at 7:20 a.m., middle school K-8 schools at 8:10 a.m., and elementary schools at 9 a.m. Some students will be walking to bus stops in the dark on a daily basis as the days grow shorter, particularly students who meet the bus at the stop near State Road 60 and Rollins Ranch Road, scheduled for 5:51 a.m., according to Dr. Kyra Schafte, executive director of the school district's strategic communications and marketing.

The School District and Indian River County Sheriff's Office urge all parents, students, and motorists to be cautious and observe rules and laws pertaining to school bus safety. Sheriff Eric Flowers said in a video posted on the sheriff's office Facebook page that all schools are changing and there will be new challenges with drop-offs, pickups, and buses. He asked parents to be patient during drop-off periods as new students entering the schools are entering through metal detectors.

At multi-lane paved roads without a raised median or physical barrier, vehicles traveling in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped to pick up or discharge children. The same rule applies to two-lane paved roads. As of May 1, Florida began issuing citations for illegal passing of a stopped school bus with stop arm extended and red lights flashing, with a $225 fine for the offense. For a second or subsequent offense within five years, the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles may suspend a driver's license for 90 days up to six months.

Parents who drive their children to bus stops should park a safe distance away from buses during both morning pickup and afternoon drop-off to help maintain clear visibility and safe loading areas, Schafte said. Families should remind students to wait until the school bus has come to a complete stop and the stop arm is fully extended before approaching or crossing the street. Transportation details are available on the Indian River County schools webpage at www.indianriverschools.org/o/sdirc/page/transportation, as well as the district's Facebook and Instagram accounts.

INDIAN RIVER COUNTY – Public school for all students in Indian River County begins on Monday, Aug. High schools open their doors to students at 7:20 a.m.; middle school K-8 schools at 8:10 a.m.; and elementary schools at 9 a.m. That means many students could be walking to bus stops sometimes in the dark on a on a daily basis as the days grow shorter. That is especially true for students who meet the bus at the stop near State Road 60 and Rollins Ranch Road, scheduled for 5:51 a.m., according to Dr. Kyra Schafte, executive director of the school district’s strategic communications and marketing. “Parents who drive their children to bus stops should park a safe distance away from buses during both morning pickup and afternoon drop off to help maintain clear visibility and safe loading areas,” she said in a statement. “We also encourage families to remind students to wait until the school bus has come to a complete stop and the stop arm is fully extended before approaching or crossing the street.” Transportation details are available on the Indian River County schools webpage at www.indianriverschools.org/o/sdirc/page/transportation , as well as the district s Facebook and Instagram accounts. The School District and Indian River County Sheriff’s Office urge all parents/students/motorists to be cautious and observe rules and laws pertaining to school bus safety throughout the 2026-27 school year. “There will be new challenges with drop offs, pickups, buses,” Sheriff Eric Flowers said in a video posted on the sheriff’s office’s Facebook page. “All the schools are changing and we want to make sure your kids are safe. We’ve got measures in place to make sure that it is a smooth beginning to the school year.” “Please be patient as during drop off periods as new students entering the schools are entering through metal detectors,” he said. “All of the safety measures we have in place will take some time for everyone to get used to.” School district officials offer these tips that parents are encouraged to review with their children regarding bus safety: * Have the child arrive at the bus stop at least 10 minutes early. * Supervise younger children while they wait for the bus. * Teach children to stay well off the roadway until the bus comes to a complete stop. * Remind children to wait for the driver’s signal before crossing the street. * Ensure backpacks, clothing, and drawstrings cannot get caught in bus handrails or doors. When walking to a bus stop, children should: * Make eye contact with the driver before crossing the street * Cross at least 10 feet in front of the bus. * Never cross behind a school bus. At bus stops, students should: * Stand at least 10 feet away from the roadway while waiting. * Never play or run near traffic. * Stay out of the bus’s ‘danger zone’—the area around the front sides, and rear where the driver may not see anyone. * If something is dropped near the bus, tell the driver instead of reaching under the bus. When on the bus, students should: * Stay seated in assigned seats and wear seat belts (when equipped) while the bus is moving. * Keep hands, arms, and head inside the bus. * Keep aisles clear of backpacks and personal items. * Speak quietly so the driver can focus on driving safely. * Do not eat, drink or throw objects on the bus. * Follow the driver’s instructions at all times. “Motorists also play an important role by slowing down, remaining alert in school zones and neighborhoods, and always stopping when required by (state) law for a school bus displaying its stop arm and flashing red lights,” Schafte said. hero.headline: Martin County firefighters rescue tree trimmer trapped 40 feet in air in Stuart
hero.body:
Martin County Fire Rescue crews on Saturday afternoon freed a tree trimmer who became trapped about 40 feet in the air after his lift stopped working in Stuart. Firefighters were dispatched around 1 p.m. to find the man stuck on the lift, which had stopped moving up and down while he was trimming trees in the area.

Limited access for a ladder forced crews to use a specialized high-angle rescue approach. Firefighters first removed nearby tree limbs, then used a series of high-angle rescue maneuvers to secure the man, transfer his weight and carefully bring him to the ground.

Paramedics evaluated the man once he reached the ground and determined he had minor injuries. The man declined transportation to the hospital.

Martin County Fire Rescue credited C-Shift crews from Heavy Rescue 23, Battalion 2, EMS 2 and EMS 22 for completing the rescue.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie man arrested on animal cruelty charge after video shows dog being kicked
hero.body:
Ricky Lee Schieferstein, 68, of Port St. Lucie was arrested on August 6 on an animal cruelty charge and remains in the St. Lucie County Jail on a $7,500 bond as of August 7. The arrest followed the circulation of a video on social media that appeared to show the abuse of a small dog.

The investigation began after numerous community members shared the video and tagged the St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office across its social media platforms. The information was turned over to the sheriffs office criminal investigations division. Detective Dawn Dale developed probable cause through her investigation and obtained an arrest warrant to charge Schieferstein with animal cruelty.

In the 16-second video posted on the sheriffs office Facebook page with a viewer discretion warning, a man can be seen walking behind a dog at a concrete pool and yelling out, out, out in the grass several times. The man kicks the dog in its right hip at least once before the dog and the man went out of range. The source of the video is not clear.

The St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office stated in a Facebook posting that it appreciates the publics assistance in bringing the incident to its attention. The sheriffs office reminded residents that the fastest and most effective way to report a crime in progress or suspicious activity is by calling 911, noting that social media platforms are not monitored continuously and should never be relied upon to report emergencies or crimes requiring an immediate law enforcement response.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie police investigate campaign sign disputes involving mayoral candidates
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police are investigating two separate incidents involving mayoral campaign signs being removed or tampered with, occurring two days apart and about a mile from each other. The incidents involve incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin and her challenger Steven Giordano in the August election race.

Surveillance footage shows a woman removing one of Mayor Shannon Martin's campaign signs on SW Thanksgiving Avenue on Wednesday night. Police say the footage also shows Giordano at the scene. Giordano stated that the homeowner had given his volunteer permission to remove the sign.

Another incident occurred early Friday morning on SW Thornhill Drive, where Giordano said he witnessed someone vandalizing his campaign sign. Police later identified the individual as Aaron Martin, the mayor's husband and a lieutenant with the Port St. Lucie Police Department. Officers said homeowners had separately granted permission for campaign signs to be placed on the property, and a language barrier may have caused confusion about the signs.

Police emphasized that the fact that the mayor's husband is a lieutenant will not affect the investigation. Shannon Martin addressed the incidents on social media Friday evening, stating that at no time did her husband steal or vandalize Giordano's sign and that the sign remained at the location. She called Giordano's allegations of burglary and vandalism completely false.

cards.headline: F-bombs fly in confrontation over Port St. Lucie campaign signs
cards.teaser: A profanity-laced confrontation was captured on video between mayoral challenger Steve Giordano and the husband of incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin.
cards.body:
As the August election approaches, tensions are rising between the two political camps as incumbent Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin faces challenger Steve Giordano in the race for mayor. The incidents prompted the Port St. Lucie Police Department to launch investigations into two separate cases involving campaign signs, one of which led to a confrontation.

During the overnight hours Friday, Aug. 7, Giordano told CBS12 News that he and his campaign manager were putting up signs near Southwest Airoso Boulevard and Southwest Thornhill Drive. Giordano said he saw a man remove a sign from the ground and throw it. Giordano then grabbed his cellphone and began recording the encounter. The man appears to be Shannon Martin's husband, Aaron Martin, a lieutenant with the Port St. Lucie Police Department. Video shows a profanity-laced confrontation between Giordano and Martin, with the two shouting at each other and making accusations about campaign signs being placed in the community without property owners' permission.

Police said investigators learned that one homeowner had given permission for one campaign sign to be placed on the property, while another resident of the home, who has limited English proficiency, told members of the opposing campaign they could also place a sign there. Investigators said the language barrier contributed to the confrontation over the campaign signs and whether the previously placed sign could be moved or removed. At this time, police said there is no indication that any campaign signs involved in the incident were stolen or intentionally damaged.

hero.headline: Martin County schools open Monday with new school bus safety measures and earlier start times
hero.body:
The 2026-2027 school year begins Monday, Aug. 10 for all students in Martin County, with 12 elementary schools opening at 7:40 a.m., four high schools including Indiantown High School charter school starting at 8:30 a.m., and five middle schools beginning at 9:20 a.m. The earlier elementary school start times mean many students will be walking to bus stops in the dark on a daily basis as the days grow shorter, particularly Jensen Beach Elementary students who meet the bus at the stop at Southeast Aster Lane and Southeast Astorwood Terrace at 6:10 a.m., according to Martin School District bus transportation schedules.

The Martin County School District is urging parents, students and motorists to observe school bus safety rules throughout the 2026-27 school year. Students should arrive at their bus stop 5 to 10 minutes before their scheduled pickup time, remain off the roadway while waiting, and follow the bus driver's instructions when boarding, exiting, or crossing the street, said Kirstie Germaine, coordinator of public information community relations. She encouraged families to review their child's bus stop location and schedule before the first day of school and ensure younger students have appropriate supervision at the bus stop.

Florida law requires drivers to stop for a school bus displaying flashing red lights and an extended stop arm on two-lane roads and on multi-lane roads without a raised median or physical barrier. As of May 1, Florida began issuing citations for illegal passing of a stopped school bus with stop arm extended and red lights flashing, with a $225 fine for the offense. For a second or subsequent offense within five years, the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles may suspend a driver's license for 90 days up to six months.

The Martin County School District's transportation page at www.martinschools.org/page/transportation provides information including links to download bus routes, bus stop rules, and safety guidance. The page also has instructions on downloading MyReaXium app, which gives parents details on the location of the school bus which will pick up and drop off their children. Parents are encouraged to supervise younger children while they wait for the bus, remind children to wait for the driver's signal before crossing the street, and ensure that backpacks, clothing, and drawstrings cannot get caught in bus handrails or doors.

School district officials offer these tips that parents are encouraged to review with their children regarding bus safety: • Supervise younger children while they wait for the bus. • Remind children to wait for the driver’s signal before crossing the street. • Ensure that backpacks, clothing, and drawstrings cannot get caught in bus handrails or doors. When walking to a bus stop, children should: • Make eye contact with the driver before crossing the street • Cross at least 10 feet in front of the bus. • Never cross behind a school bus. At bus stops, students should: • Stand at least 10 feet away from the roadway while waiting. • Never play or run near traffic. • Stay out of the bus’s ‘danger zone’—the area around the front sides, and rear where the driver may not see anyone. • If something is dropped near the bus, tell the driver instead of reaching under the bus. When on the bus, students should: • Stay seated in assigned seats and wear seat belts (when equipped) while the bus is moving. • Keep hands, arms, and head inside the bus. • Keep aisles clear of backpacks and personal items. • Speak quietly so the driver can focus on driving safely. • Do not eat, drink or throw objects on the bus. • Follow the driver’s instructions at all times. Drivers are required by Florida law to stop for a school bus displaying flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, according to the state Department of Transportation’s web site. Drivers also must stop on two-lane roads and on multi-lane roads without a raised median or physical barrier, according to the web site. As of May 1, Florida began issuing citations for illegal passing of a stopped school bus with stop arm extended and red lights flashing, with a $225 fine for the offense. For a second or subsequent offense within five years, the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles may suspend your driver’s license for 90 days up to 6 months A driver does not have to stop when traveling in the opposite direction only if the roadway is divided by a raised median, a physical barrier or an unpaved median at least five feet wide, according to the DOT web site. In addition, the driver’s cell phone must be “hands-free” in a school zone. Using a wireless communications device in a handheld manner while driving in a designated school crossing, school zone, or active work zone area is against the law, according to the DOT web site. hero.headline: Port St. Lucie police investigate campaign sign confrontations between mayor and challenger
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police are investigating two separate incidents involving mayoral campaign signs being removed or tampered with, occurring two days apart and about a mile from each other. The confrontations involve incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin and challenger Steven Giordano in the race ahead of the August election.

Surveillance footage shows a woman removing one of Mayor Shannon Martin's campaign signs on SW Thanksgiving Avenue on Wednesday night. Police say the footage also shows Giordano at the scene. Giordano stated that the homeowner had given his volunteer permission to remove the sign. Another incident occurred early Friday morning on SW Thornhill Drive, where Giordano said he witnessed someone vandalizing his campaign sign. Police later identified the individual as Aaron Martin, the mayor's husband and a lieutenant with the Port St. Lucie Police Department. Video shows a profanity-laced confrontation between Giordano and Aaron Martin, with the two shouting at each other and making accusations about campaign signs being placed in the community without property owners' permission.

Officers said homeowners had separately granted permission for campaign signs to be placed on the property, and a language barrier may have caused confusion about the signs. Investigators learned that one homeowner had given permission for one campaign sign to be placed on the property, while another resident of the home, who has limited English proficiency, told members of the opposing campaign they could also place a sign there. On Friday evening, Shannon Martin addressed the incidents on social media, stating that she was aware of recent incidents involving the unauthorized removal of her campaign signs over several days. She said some of her signs had been taken down without permission and replaced with Giordano's signs. Martin stated that at no time did her husband steal Giordano's sign nor did he damage or vandalize it, and that the sign remained at the location.

Police emphasized that the fact that the mayor's husband is a lieutenant will not affect the investigation. The Port St. Lucie Police Department said it remains committed to conducting a fair, impartial and fact-based investigation. At this time, police said there is no indication that any campaign signs involved in the incident were stolen or intentionally damaged. Detectives are reviewing physical evidence, speaking with witnesses and verifying statements provided to investigators. The investigations remain active.

cards.headline: 77-year-old Port St. Lucie man found dead in pond near his home
cards.teaser: Michael Joseph Kramer, 77, was found unresponsive in a pond directly across the street from his residence on SW Mockingbird Drive.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police are investigating the death of a 77-year-old man who was found in a pond on Friday. Around 1:18 p.m., officers were called to a residence on SW Mockingbird Drive in reference to a missing adult who was later identified as Michael Joseph Kramer, 77.

The investigation revealed that Kramer was last seen by his wife inside of their residence at around 10:00 p.m. Thursday. When Kramer's wife woke up at approximately 7:00 a.m. on Friday, Kramer was nowhere to be found despite all of his personal belongings remaining in the residence. After an extensive search of the area, police located an unresponsive man that matched Kramer's description in a pond directly across the street from the residence at around 2:00 p.m. The Port St. Lucie Police Department Dive Team recovered Kramer from the water, and he was pronounced deceased. The circumstances surrounding his death remain unclear, but no indications of foul play seem apparent.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man arrested after video shows alleged abuse of small dog
cards.teaser: Ricky Lee Shieferstein, 68, was charged with animal cruelty after video showed him appearing to kick a small dog in his backyard.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie man was arrested following an investigation into a social media video that shows a man abusing a small dog, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Video from the Sheriff's Office shows Ricky Lee Shieferstein, 68, appearing to kick a small dog in his backyard near a pool.

The video made rounds on social media, and the outrage sparked an investigation from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Following the investigation, the Sheriff's Office's findings gave detectives probable cause to charge Shieferstein with animal cruelty. Shieferstein is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $7,500 bond.

Voters can cast their ballots at any of the designated early voting sites in the county. This differs from Election Day, when voters must go to their assigned polling place.

Voters should bring a current, valid photo ID with a signature. If the photo ID does not include a signature, a second form of identification may be required. Election officials recommend checking voter information and reviewing sample ballots before heading to the polls.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie postpones Riverland sports complex rezoning after Tradition residents protest
hero.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council voted unanimously on July 27 to postpone a rezoning request for a 135,000-square-foot indoor and outdoor sports recreation complex in the Riverland area after dozens of Tradition-area homeowners packed City Chambers in protest. The council tabled the request from Riverland/Kennedy II LLC until August 24 to give the developer time to hold a neighborhood meeting with concerned residents. The developer GL Homes is seeking to rezone approximately 33.23 acres south of Southwest Discovery Way and east of Southwest Sundance Vista Boulevard from St. Lucie County Agricultural to Riverland-West Sports Recreation Master Planned Unit Development.

Residents who spoke at the hearing said they purchased their homes with the understanding that the parcel would be a city park, not a commercial recreation facility. Southwest River Rock Road resident Jim Riordan told the council GL Homes has 1,300 other acres where they could build the complex and that the company is already advertising the fitness center in sales materials for new parcels. Harriet Gallas said she was told when she bought her house there would be a park over the berm next to her property. She told the council the planned 72 pickleball courts, bocci courts, tennis courts, dog park and RV park would destroy her quality of life through noise pollution.

Planning Zoning Director Mary Savage-Dunham told the council the rezoning is consistent with the city comprehensive plan and a pre-existing Development of Regional Impact for the area. The site is designated Neighborhood Village Commercial, which allows a mixture of residential and non-residential uses including commercial offices, personal and household services, institutional facilities, public facilities, parks, playgrounds and similar services. Land Use Attorney Azlina Goldstein, representing the applicant, initially resisted postponing the request and said details about landscaping, buffers and specific indoor and outdoor features would be addressed during the site-plan process, not the rezoning.

Mayor Shannon Martin asked Goldstein if GL Homes would be willing to meet with residents to address their concerns. Vice-Mayor Jolien Caraballo urged Goldstein to table the request, saying residents did not comprehend the quasi-judicial rezoning process. After loud protest from the audience, the council voted to postpone the hearing until August 24. City Attorney Richard Berrios explained that the rezoning is a quasi-judicial process limited to sworn testimony and facts applied to the specific rezoning request, with details about landscaping and specific features reserved for the site-plan process.
hero.article_text: The location and aerial maps of the 33.23-acre parcel that G.L. Homes wants to rezone in order to build a 135,000-square-foot indoor and outdoor recreation area known as the Riverland-West Sports Recreation complex. Because so many residents both emailed the city and spoke out in protest during the July 27 quasi-judicial rezoning hearing, the City Council voted unanimously that day to table the request until Aug. 24 to give the applicant time to hold a neighborhood meeting. LUCIE – City Council members found themselves defending their actions to frustrated Tradition-area residents July 27, prompting them to table a quasi-judicial rezoning request from the developer of the Riverland/Kennedy Development of Regional Impact. The delay will give the developer’s representatives time to meet with area homeowners and address their concerns. Planner Francis Forman introduced the controversial agenda item that evening to a packed Chambers. “The item before you is the Riverland-West Sports Recreation Master Planned Unit Development rezoning,” he said. “The applicant is Azlina Goldstein with Riverland/Kennedy II LLC. This site is located south of Southwest Discovery Way and east of Southwest Sundance Vista Boulevard. The request is to rezone approximately 33.23 acres from St. Lucie County Agricultural to Riverland-West Sports Recreation MPUD.” Forman proceeded to provide more details on the GL Homes request to develop the site in a manner that many Riverland homeowners claim is different than what was planned when they purchased their properties years ago. “This site is designated Neighborhood Village Commercial, which allows a mixture of residential and non-residential uses such as commercial and offices, personal and household services, institutional, public facilities, parks, playgrounds and similar services,” he explained. “Any Neighborhood Village Commercial area must contain at least two of those uses. Currently the Riverland-West Sports Recreation MPUD is proposing to provide about 135,000 square feet of indoor recreation with some commercial as well as some outdoor RV/boat storage areas.” Because the city had received numerous emails from nearby residents in opposition, Vice-Mayor Jolien Caraballo immediately asked City Attorney Richard Berrios to describe the formalities of the quasi-judicial process. “This is a rezoning, which is limited to what Mr. Forman presented,” Berrios said. “Not part of it are things like landscaping, indoor and outdoor features and specifics of what it will ultimately be. Those things are better suited for the site-plan process. As far as the process here, the legislators take off their legislative hats and put on their judge robes, and it’s limited to taking sworn testimony and the facts presented and applying them to a specific problem.” Councilman Anthony Bonna, however, believed more information was needed for the area residents. “Can you go into more detail about what evidence is allowed to be weighed [and] is a rezoning discretionary?” he asked. While Berrios admitted the Council’s hands were tied as far as any pre-existing DRI entitlements, he deferred Councilman Bonna’s question to Planning Zoning Director Mary Savage-Dunham. The latter emphasized the legal framework of controlling agreements and city codes. A pre-existing Development of Regional Impact (DRI) is a large-scale project approved under older Florida growth laws that retains vested development rights despite later changes to local plans or the elimination of the state’s formal DRI program. “The DRI document talks about what’s going to be built there,” Savage-Dunam said. “We also have the comprehensive plan. As staff testified, this rezoning was found to be consistent with the comprehensive plan, [which] follows the DRI. Those are the road maps that guide development in that section of the city. So, you would be looking at the totality of what the applicant submitted showing their intended uses there and how that aligns with the comp plan and the DRI.” Vice-Mayor Caraballo then chimed back in with her own perspective. “If you’re confused, I understand,” she said. “It’s not our process – it’s the way it’s legally required by the state. It’s definitely not the simplest thing for anybody to understand.” After the applicant’s contracted Land Use Attorney Goldstein provided her own presentation, 10 nearby homeowners aired their complaints, beginning with Southwest River Rock Road resident Jim Riordan. “My property is located at the southern end of the proposed Riverland-West Sports Recreation Center,” he said. “I spoke at the July 7 Planning Board meeting, and the chairman encouraged me to meet with Ms. At that time, I gave her our primary concerns with the project. On Friday, she did contact me, but none of those concerns were addressed. What she did say was exactly what she said right now: This is not the time – the time is later – but we feel this is the time before we move forward.” Riordan pointed out that GL Homes had “1,300 other acres where they could build this complex.” “GL has already sold parcels in the new section advertising the fitness center,” he continued. “So, I guess it’s a done deal based on this picture and what they’re advertising. We purchased our property, as well as every citizen here, from The Grove with the understanding that this parcel will be a city park. Now they’re basically trying to make this something different.” Both Harriet Gallas and her husband Lawrence agreed. “We chose to move here for quality of life,” the former said. “When we bought our house, we were told there was going to be a park over the berm next to us. They’re [now] talking 72 pickleball courts, bocci courts, tennis courts, a dog park and RV park, and that’s going to destroy my quality of life. Noise pollution’s a real thing: It causes stress, and pickleball is loud, stabbing and sharp. I respectfully beg you to not pass this rezoning.” The other residents echoed similar fears, resulting in more staff explanations and Council debate until Mayor Shannon Martin asked Goldstein a pivotal question. “Has their been a public meeting with the neighbors with regard to this issue?” she asked. Riordan regarding the issue of the buffer,” Goldstein responded. That response gave Mayor Martin the impetus she needed. “Being that there are so many concerns from the residents, is GL willing to have a meeting with the residents in order to address the issues?” she prodded. Goldstein, however, resisted the delay at first. “This is a straight-forward rezoning,” she insisted. “We don’t have all those details yet for the site plan because that’s not this process. hero.headline: Port St. Lucie mayor's husband confronts opponent over campaign signs in profanity-laced clash
hero.teaser: A profanity-laced confrontation over campaign signs erupted overnight Friday between mayoral candidate Steve Giordano and the husband of incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin, prompting a police investigation.
hero.body:
Mayoral candidate Steve Giordano says he and his campaign manager were putting up signs in Port St. Lucie during the overnight hours on Friday, Aug. 7, when he saw a man take a sign out of the ground and throw it. Giordano grabbed his cell phone and began recording the incident. The man appears to be Shannon Martin's husband, Aaron Martin, a lieutenant in Port St. Lucie's Police Department. Video shows a profanity-laced confrontation between Giordano and the other man, with both shouting at each other and making accusations about putting up signs in the community without property owners' permission.

The Port St. Lucie Police Department says it is actively investigating two separate reports involving political campaign signs that occurred this week in the city. Officers responded to the reported incidents, documented the scenes, collected available evidence, and began interviewing those involved. Detectives are reviewing physical evidence, speaking with witnesses, and verifying statements provided to investigators.

Mayor Shannon Martin said in a statement that her campaign is aware of recent incidents involving the unauthorized removal of her campaign signs at different locations over several days. Signs were taken down without permission and replaced with Giordano's signs, Martin said. "In response, my husband simply restored the signs that had been removed," Martin said. "At no time were my opponent's signs stolen or damaged, one small sign was temporarily moved and put back in the ground." Martin and Giordano are running in the August election to determine who will hold the mayor's office.

cards.headline: Tradition Lakes K-8 opening delayed one week, leaving St. Lucie parents scrambling for child care
cards.body:
St. Lucie County's new Tradition Lakes K-8 school will not open on Monday, Aug. 10 as planned, pushing the start date back one week to Aug. 17 and leaving approximately 1,100 enrolled students and their families scrambling to arrange last-minute child care. St. Lucie Public Schools announced the delay on Thursday, just four days before the originally scheduled opening.

Superintendent Dr. Prince said he made the decision after personally inspecting the school site at 10701 SW Sundance Vista Boulevard in Port St. Lucie and consulting with teachers and staff. Prince said he did not want students to navigate what essentially remained a construction zone on their first day. "That's not the first impression that I wanted to make where you're kind of walking and you're kind of part of a construction zone and I just didn't think it was fair," Prince said. "After kind of seeing things for myself, I was really worried that when people rush they make mistakes and I just felt like it was in our best interest to take a pause."

Parents expressed frustration at the short notice. Asia Shouford, a working mother of four children, said the timing completely disrupted her carefully planned arrangements. "I was honestly annoyed, because school starts on Monday, it was Thursday when we got that call. You could have told us a week ago," Shouford said. "Working mom, four kids, I have two little ones at home. I already had everything planned to start on Monday and now I don't know what we're going to do." Parent Taylor Atkins said the delay put families in a tough situation with limited options on short notice. "It's hard because he can't go back to summer camp. It's closed it's another school, you know, they're going to be starting," Atkins said.

The school district said the one-week delay will not impact overall instructional time and the school's academic calendar will remain unchanged. To help working families manage the unexpected delay, the district is coordinating with the Boys and Girls Club and the YMCA to offer affordable child care options during the interim week. Open House is scheduled for Friday, Aug. 14, from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., where families can meet teachers and tour the campus before the first day.

hero.headline: Costco in Stuart reopens after electrical fire, refrigeration still down
hero.body:
Costco at 3173 Kanner Highway in Stuart reopened Friday following an electrical fire that temporarily closed the store on Thursday. The Stuart Police Department says store management confirmed only dry goods are available for purchase because the refrigeration unit remains non-operational.

The Stuart Police Department reported the electrical fire has been extinguished. Shoppers and travelers were asked to avoid the area while the store was closed Thursday.

The store is now open but customers cannot purchase refrigerated or frozen items until the refrigeration system is restored. The Stuart Police Department shared the update from store management about the limited inventory.

The Costco location serves Stuart and surrounding Martin County communities. The electrical fire forced the temporary closure on Thursday before the store reopened with limited services Friday.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Mets fall 17-3 to Daytona as Tortugas score 11 unanswered runs at Clover Park
hero.body:
The Daytona Tortugas scored 11 unanswered runs over the final three innings Thursday to defeat the St. Lucie Mets 17-3 at Clover Park. The Mets cut the Daytona lead to 6-3 in the fifth inning with three doubles, including back-to-back RBI doubles by John Smith III and Julio Zayas. The Tortugas broke the game open in the seventh inning, taking advantage of six walks issued by Mets relievers Jean Brito and Luis Sotillo to score six runs and build a 12-3 lead.

Daytona added five more runs in the eighth inning off Zayas, who pitched the final two innings for the Mets after serving as the designated hitter. Zayas pitched a scoreless ninth inning and induced a double play. The Mets scored first on a RBI single by Reed Stallman in the second inning, but Tortugas starter Mason Morris escaped further damage with the bases loaded by starting a 1-2-3 double play off the broken bat of Kooper Schulte.

The Tortugas used that momentum to score five runs on five hits off Mets starter Jose Lopez in the third inning. Bernard Moon hit a two-run double in the inning, his Florida State League-leading 28th double. Lopez pitched 5.1 innings overall and gave up six runs on seven hits with one walk and six strikeouts. It was the longest outing by a Mets pitcher since the first game of the second half on June 19.

Elian Pea went 2 for 5 with a double, his third straight two-hit game. Smith III finished 2 for 4 with a double and RBI. The Mets, now 14-23 in the second half and 47-56 overall, continue their series against the Tortugas at Clover Park on Friday. All veterans and active duty military receive free admission courtesy of LYNQ Real Estate, and kids 14 and under can run the bases after the game.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie man arrested on animal cruelty charge after video circulates on social media
hero.body:
Ricky Lee Schieferstein, 68, of Port St. Lucie was arrested on Aug. 6 on an animal cruelty charge following the circulation of a video on social media that appeared to show the abuse of a small dog. Schieferstein was being held at the St. Lucie County Jail as of Aug. 7 on a $7,500 bond, according to the jail website.

The investigation began after numerous members of the community shared the video and tagged the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office across its social media platforms, according to the sheriff's office Facebook posting. The information was then turned over to the sheriff's office criminal investigations division for investigation. Detective Dawn Dale developed probable cause through her investigation and obtained an arrest warrant to charge Schieferstein with animal cruelty.

In the 16-second video posted on the sheriff's office Facebook page with a viewer discretion warning, a man can be seen walking behind a dog at a concrete pool and yelling out, out, out ... in the grass several times and kicking the dog in its right hip at least once before the dog and the man went out of range.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office stated in its Facebook posting that it appreciates the public's assistance in bringing this incident to its attention. However, the sheriff's office also reminded residents that the fastest and most effective way to report a crime in progress or suspicious activity is by calling 911. While the sheriff's office actively monitors its social media platforms, they are not monitored continuously and should never be relied upon to report emergencies or crimes requiring an immediate law enforcement response.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Kings Landing development faces new delay as developer seeks $15 million to finish Marriott hotel
hero.teaser: Live Oak Development, the secondary developer on Fort Pierce's Kings Landing project, told city commissioners they are $15 million short of the $60 million needed to complete the Marriott hotel and restaurant portion of the project.
hero.body:
The Kings Landing development in Fort Pierce is facing another delay as Live Oak Development, the secondary developer on the project, told city commissioners they are $15 million short of the $60 million needed to complete the Marriott hotel and restaurant portion of the project. City commissioners are divided on what to do next. Live Oak Development told commissioners the $15 million shortfall is due in part to rising construction costs. CEO Paul Bertozzi said the company has seen construction costs continue to balloon across multiple industries, and that is a portion of the cause of the delta being created.

City leaders said developers initially asked the city to cover the gap through a loan or grant. Commissioner Michael Broderick said that request was denied, and the city does not have $15 million. Live Oak Development is now asking for 180 days to find the money through private sources. Bertozzi told commissioners the outreach has already begun, and the company is looking at friends and families and investment and private equity versus institutional investors. Broderick said he believes trying to reclaim the property through legal action would be expensive and time-consuming, and would rather give developers the time they are asking for.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie police investigate death of 77-year-old man found in pond near his home
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police are investigating the death of 77-year-old Michael Joseph Kramer, who was found unresponsive in a pond near his home on Friday afternoon after being reported missing earlier that day.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police are investigating the death of 77-year-old Michael Joseph Kramer, who was found unresponsive in a pond near his home on Friday afternoon after being reported missing earlier that day. At approximately 1:18 p.m. Friday, officers responded to a residence on the 1400 block of SW Mockingbird Drive regarding a missing adult. Kramer was last seen by his wife inside their home at approximately 10 p.m. Thursday. The following morning, Kramer was no longer inside the residence. Kramer's personal belongings, including his shoes, wallet, and cellphone, were still inside the home.

Kramer's wife searched for him and contacted local hospitals before reporting him missing to law enforcement at approximately 1:18 p.m. Officers began searching the neighborhood and, during the canvass, located an unresponsive person in a pond directly across the street from Kramer's residence at approximately 2 p.m. The individual and clothing matched Kramer's description. Port St. Lucie Police Department Dive Team recovered Kramer from the water near the shoreline of the pond, where he was confirmed deceased. The circumstances surrounding Kramer's death remain under investigation. Police said there are no known indications of foul play at this preliminary stage of the investigation.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie police investigate two separate campaign sign incidents involving Mayor Martin's husband
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Department released an update Friday on two separate investigations involving political campaign signs, both occurring this week in the area of SW Airoso Boulevard. The first incident occurred August 5 near the intersection of SW Airoso Boulevard and SW Thanksgiving Avenue, where a Port St. Lucie Police sergeant observed Steven Giordano and an unidentified adult female near political campaign signs at a residence and initiated an investigation after one campaign sign was found on the ground while another had been placed in the yard. Detectives reviewed surveillance video from the area, which appears to show Giordano and the unidentified adult female arrive at the residence, approach campaign signs displayed in the yard, and interact with the signage. The video further appears to show the unidentified female remove a campaign sign supporting Mayor Shannon Martin before a different campaign sign was placed in the yard.

The second incident occurred August 7 near SW Airoso Boulevard and SW Thornhill Drive, where officers responded to a disturbance involving political campaign signs. During the investigation, officers learned that Aaron Martin and Steven Giordano were involved in a verbal confrontation regarding the placement and movement of campaign signs at a nearby residence. Officers reviewed video recordings provided by the involved parties, which depict Martin and Giordano engaged in a verbal confrontation regarding the placement and movement of political campaign signs at the residence. The confrontation occurred after Giordano says he saw a man take a sign out of the ground and throw it, according to CBS12 News. The man in the video appears to be Aaron Martin, Shannon Martin's husband and a lieutenant in Port St. Lucie's Police Department.

Investigators interviewed the homeowners and learned that both residents believed they had separately granted permission for campaign signs to be placed on the property. Officers determined that one homeowner communicated permission for one campaign's sign, while another resident of the home, who has limited English proficiency, separately conveyed permission to individuals associated with the opposing campaign. Investigators believe the language barrier contributed to a misunderstanding regarding which campaign signs were authorized to be displayed and whether previously placed signs could be moved or replaced. The preliminary investigation indicates that both individuals believed they had permission from residents of the property to place campaign signs. Information related to the placement of the campaign signs has been forwarded to the City of Port St. Lucie Code Compliance for review.

The Port St. Lucie Police Department acknowledged that Aaron Martin is employed by the department. The department said the fact that Martin is a department employee will not influence the investigative process, and the investigation will be conducted fairly, impartially, and in accordance with department policy. The department said that should the investigation identify any potential policy violations involving a department employee, the matter will be handled in accordance with established department procedures. Any related administrative review will proceed following the completion of the ongoing criminal investigation. Mayor Shannon Martin said in a statement that her campaign is aware of recent incidents involving the unauthorized removal of her campaign signs at different locations over several days, and that her husband simply restored the signs that had been removed.

cards.headline: Road rage confrontation leads to four-vehicle crash on U.S. 1 in Port St. Lucie, one arrested
cards.teaser: A road rage confrontation erupted into a violent four-vehicle crash on U.S. 1 Wednesday, leaving four injured and a Port St. Lucie man arrested.
cards.body:
A road rage confrontation erupted into a violent four-vehicle crash on U.S. 1 Wednesday, leaving four injured and a Port St. Lucie man arrested. Officers with the Port St. Lucie Police Department responded around 6:45 p.m. to the intersection of South U.S. Highway 1 and SE Lyngate Drive/SE Tiffany Avenue, where investigators determined that a red Harley-Davidson motorcycle and a black Ford Super Duty pickup truck were involved in an ongoing road rage incident. Officer Brittany McNally with the Port St. Lucie Police Department said the two vehicles were involved in an active road rage incident just prior to the crash, based on dash camera and witness statements collected.

Detectives say the pickup, driven by 54-year-old Kevin Lonergan, was pursuing the motorcycle as both vehicles traveled northbound on U.S. 1 and approached the intersection. According to witness statements and dash-camera video, the motorcycle entered the intersection against a red light and collided with a black Chevrolet Silverado, throwing the 31-year-old rider from the bike. Police say Lonergan then entered the intersection against the red signal, struck the ejected motorcyclist, and crashed head-on into a blue Toyota RAV4. The motorcyclist and two people inside the RAV4 were taken to Lawnwood Medical Center. The Silverado driver was transported to St. Lucie Medical Center.

Investigators say the motorcyclist suffered serious injuries, including a brain bleed and facial fractures, and lost consciousness after the crash. He remains hospitalized in stable condition. Based on witness statements, dash-camera video and the investigation, police arrested Lonergan for two counts of reckless driving causing serious bodily injury and one count of reckless driving causing injury. The investigative findings indicate that the pickup truck was actively pursuing that motorcyclist just moments prior to that crash, McNally said. After being medically cleared, Lonergan was booked into the St. Lucie County Jail. The intersection remained closed for hours while investigators processed the scene before all lanes reopened around 2 a.m.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man arrested after video shows him kicking small dog
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie man was arrested following an investigation into a social media video that shows a man abusing a small dog.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie man was arrested following an investigation into a social media video that shows a man abusing a small dog, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Video from the sheriff's office shows Ricky Lee Shieferstein, 68, appearing to kick a small dog in his backyard near a pool. The video made rounds on social media, and the outrage sparked an investigation from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office.

Following the investigation, the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office's findings gave detectives probable cause to charge Shieferstein with animal cruelty. The sheriff's office says that Shieferstein is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $7,500 bond.

cards.headline: Deputies execute search warrant at Fort Pierce home tied to $7 million Southern Truss fraud investigation
cards.teaser: A large law enforcement presence descended on a Fort Pierce neighborhood Tuesday morning as detectives executed a search warrant connected to an alleged fraud scheme that investigators say cost Southern Truss Companies nearly $7 million.
cards.body:
A large law enforcement presence descended on a Fort Pierce neighborhood Tuesday morning as detectives executed a search warrant connected to an alleged fraud scheme that investigators say cost Southern Truss Companies nearly $7 million. St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office confirmed to CBS12 News that deputies are serving a search warrant as part of the ongoing investigation into the Southern Truss fraud case. Crime scene investigators were seen outside the home of Laura Beth Grasso in the Indian River Estates neighborhood near Sunset Boulevard. Grasso was arrested July 16 along with Sheri Lynn Harrs and Tina Marie Mejia following what the sheriff's office described as a years-long scheme targeting Southern Truss Companies. Grasso has pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Investigators allege Grasso, who worked as the company's bookkeeper and comptroller, used her administrative access to bypass financial controls and funnel millions of dollars out of the business. Detectives say the money was spent on luxury vehicles, vacations, designer goods, jewelry and other personal expenses. Neighbors on Sunset Boulevard told CBS12 News they had long been suspicious of Grasso's lifestyle. Neighbor Greg Longhway said Grasso had four or five brand new trucks and got food delivery every day, four different food deliveries.

Grasso faces charges of first-degree grand theft of $100,000 or more, organized fraud of $50,000 or more, conducting an enterprise through a pattern of racketeering activity, and money laundering of $100,000 or more. Harrs and Mejia each face charges of grand theft, organized fraud and racketeering. Grasso's bond was set at a combined $1.15 million across the four charges. Prosecutors have asked a judge to hold a hearing on the legitimacy and source of any bail premium or collateral before allowing Grasso to be released from the St. Lucie County Jail.

Lucie County Sheriff's Office confirmed to CBS12 News that deputies are serving a search warrant as part of the ongoing investigation into the Southern Truss fraud case. Crime scene investigators were seen outside the home of Laura Beth Grasso in the Indian River Estates neighborhood near Sunset Boulevard. Grasso was arrested July 16 along with Sheri Lynn Harrs and Tina Marie Mejia following what the sheriff's office described as a years-long scheme targeting Southern Truss Companies. Grasso has pleaded not guilty to the charges, court records show. Investigators allege Grasso, who worked as the company's bookkeeper and comptroller, used her administrative access to bypass financial controls and funnel millions of dollars out of the business. Detectives say the money was spent on luxury vehicles, vacations, designer goods, jewelry and other personal expenses. Neighbors on Sunset Boulevard told CBS12 News they had long been suspicious of Grasso's lifestyle. They got 4 or 5 brand new trucks. They got food delivery every day, four different food deliveries. I mean, we always wondered what was going on over there," neighbor Greg Longhway said. Grasso faces charges of: First-degree grand theft of $100,000 or more Organized fraud of $50,000 or more Conducting an enterprise through a pattern of racketeering activity (RICO) Money laundering of $100,000 or more Harrs and Mejia each face charges of grand theft, organized fraud and racketeering. Grasso's bond was set at a combined $1.15 million across the four charges. Longhway said he watched deputies storm the house Tuesday morning. "Oh, they came ripping in, and the SWAT gear and everything with the guns pulled and hollering. Come out that search warrant. Come out with your hands up," he said. Prosecutors have asked a judge to hold a hearing on the legitimacy and source of any bail premium or collateral before allowing Grasso to be released from the St. Lucie County Jail, arguing in a court filing that a defendant should not be able to use money obtained through criminal activity to secure her release. Tuesday's search follows an earlier warrant served on a vehicle connected to Grasso. A judge signed that warrant July 24, authorizing detectives to search a blue 2025 Chevrolet Tahoe registered to Grasso that had been towed to the sheriff's office evidence compound the day after her arrest. According to an inventory filed with the court, deputies found roughly $8,500 in cash, a jewelry organizer with jewelry, a Louis Vuitton purse and wallet, and a loaded Smith & Wesson M&P .40 Shield pistol in the glove box. Longhway said the family largely kept to themselves. They've never said a word to anybody. They've been there for a year and a half, two years. They don't talk to anybody, which is fine; we don't care," Longhway said. "We figured something was up over there, though." The alleged scheme started to unravel after a tornado damaged the Southern Truss facility, according to the criminal complaint. With the plant largely shut down, the company's owner noticed operating costs staying suspiciously high, including fuel charges for a company jet that wasn't flying. When he confronted Grasso and told her outside forensic accountants were being brought in, investigators say server logs show she began logging into the company's financial system overnight to alter records. A forensic audit later recovered a secret "shadow ledger" on her computer, according to the complaint, tracking where the missing money had actually gone. Southern Truss also filed a civil lawsuit against the three women, alleging they carried out a coordinated scheme between 2018 and 2025 to divert company funds through unauthorized payroll payments, wire transfers and other transactions. The amended complaint alleges Grasso alone misappropriated at least $5 million, while Mejia and Harrs allegedly received hundreds of thousands more. The criminal case remains pending. Court records show a magistrate in June declined to pause the related civil case because of the criminal proceedings, instead ordering the defendants to respond to discovery by July 30 and complete depositions by Aug. Neighbors say they saw someone arrested by a SWAT team this morning. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has not confirmed any additional arrests or what investigators were searching for on Tuesday.

lead_independence.headline: Tradition Lakes K-8 opening pushed back one week, leaving 1,100 Port St. Lucie families scrambling for child care
lead_independence.lead: St. Lucie Public Schools announced Thursday that the first day of classes at Tradition Lakes K-8 school will be pushed from August 10 to August 17, affecting approximately 1,100 students enrolled at the new school. Parents received notification of the delay just four days before the originally scheduled opening, sparking frustration among families who had already arranged work schedules and child care around the initial start date. Asia Shouford, a working mother of four children, said she was honestly annoyed because school starts on Monday and the notification came on Thursday. hero.headline: Piper's Landing residents plant 6,000 mangroves to restore eroded St. Lucie River island in Martin County
hero.body:
Residents at Piper's Landing Yacht and Country Club in Martin County are planting 6,000 mangroves to restore a mangrove island next to their marina that erosion has slowly destroyed. The community spent two years cultivating the red and white mangroves in an on-site nursery before beginning the planting work in the St. Lucie River waterway.

Lisa Standing, a resident at Piper's Landing Yacht and Country Club, rallied her neighbors to take action after watching the mangroves deteriorate. The community built 10 planter pools to grow the mangroves, collecting red and white seeds from their mangrove island. Residents were at the nursery almost every day to inspect the plants, water them when needed, monitor their health, and match salinity to the river conditions.

The effort required extensive research and permitting before a single plant could go into the water. With the nursery phase complete, residents brought in Keith Rossin, CEO of Mang Consulting Services, to do the planting. Rossin said the project uses dredge fill brought up to the right elevation for the mangroves, creating mangrove habitat in a way he has never seen done before.

The thousands of small trees are expected to grow into the foundation of a new ecosystem. Standing said residents will be able to go down to the mangrove island and enjoy a beautiful lush island once the restoration is complete.
