cards.headline: Fundraiser supports Port St. Lucie firefighter who lost both parents in murder-suicide
cards.teaser: Friends, family and strangers are raising money for 30-year-old Ralphy Varela, a Palm Beach County firefighter-paramedic whose mother was killed by his father in a Port St. Lucie murder-suicide over the weekend.
cards.body:
An online fundraiser for 30-year-old Ralphy Varela has raised thousands of dollars after he lost both parents in a murder-suicide at a Port St. Lucie home over the weekend. The fundraiser has been widely shared across social media, along with a photo of Varela and his mother, Elizabeth Ortega.

Ortega, a longtime Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office communications officer, was killed Saturday at her home on Southeast Oxmoor Terrace, according to Port St. Lucie police. Investigators say her longtime partner, Ralph Varela Sr., shot her before taking his own life. Detectives say the couple had recently ended their long-term relationship but continued living together while other arrangements were being made. Police said the couple's adult son had left the home shortly before the shooting occurred.

The fundraiser was created by Jorge Uricoechea to support Ralphy Varela, who serves as a firefighter-paramedic with Palm Beach County Fire Rescue. One lifelong friend described Ortega simply as very loved. Supporters say the fundraiser is a way to honor Ortega's memory while helping her son rebuild in the days and weeks ahead.
cards.article_text: Friends, family members, and strangers across South Florida are coming together to support a Palm Beach County firefighter-paramedic who lost both of his parents in a tragic murder-suicide over the weekend. An online fundraiser for 30-year-old Ralphy Varela has already raised thousands of dollars as supporters work to help him navigate the unimaginable loss. The fundraiser has been widely shared across social media, along with a photo of Varela and his mother, Elizabeth "Liz" Ortega. Ortega, a longtime Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office communications officer, spent years helping callers through emergencies and crises. Colleagues and friends say she was deeply respected and loved by those who knew her. Related article: Newly released 911 call reveals frantic moments after Port St. Lucie murder-suicide According to Port St. Lucie police, Ortega was killed Saturday at her home. Investigators say her longtime partner, Ralph Varela Sr., shot her before taking his own life. Detectives say the couple had recently ended their long-term relationship but continued living together while other arrangements were being made. Police said the couple's adult son had left the home shortly before the shooting occurred. Neighbors called 911 after hearing gunfire. As the investigation continues, much of the community's focus has shifted to supporting Ralphy Varela, who serves as a firefighter-paramedic with Palm Beach County Fire Rescue. One lifelong friend described Ortega simply as "very loved." Supporters say the fundraiser , created by Jorge Uricoechea, is a way to honor Ortega's memory while helping her son rebuild in the days and weeks ahead.

cards.headline: 12-year-old describes hit-and-run that injured sister in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: Malachi Jenkins, 12, was with his 8-year-old sister Serenity when she was struck by a driver who fled the scene at North 25th Street and Avenue M in Fort Pierce over the weekend.
cards.body:
Malachi Jenkins, 12, said he was mad when a driver struck his 8-year-old sister Serenity and then drove off at the intersection of North 25th Street and Avenue M in Fort Pierce over the weekend. Malachi described the moments after the crash, saying Serenity was on the ground with her legs bent in different directions. People ran up to check on her, and she started crying before briefly losing consciousness and then waking back up.

Malachi said the driver initially offered to take them home but fled the scene when others approached. When he saw the other people coming and looked at Serenity, he just drove off fast, Malachi said. Police confirmed that Serenity sustained a fractured femur in the crash.

Fort Pierce police believe the driver is a man between the ages of 20 and 30 years old, driving an early 2000s gold Mercedes-Benz that may have damage to the driver's side. Detectives are reviewing surveillance footage from nearby businesses to gather more information about the incident. Anyone with information is urged to contact Fort Pierce detectives.
cards.article_text: Police in Fort Pierce are investigating a hit-and-run that injured 8-year-old Serenity Jenkins over the weekend at the intersection of North 25th Street and Avenue M. Detectives are reviewing surveillance footage from nearby businesses to gather more information about the incident. "I just think it's sad overall because it's a little girl. I mean, you have to have some type of humanity not to just drive away and not make sure she's OK; that's somebody's child," said a woman who works near the intersection where the crash occurred. Serenity’s 12-year-old brother, Malachi Jenkins, said he was with her when the crash happened. "I was mad," Malachi said. He described the moments after the crash, saying, "She was on the ground, and her legs were like this, one like that, and that's when people ran up and were checking on her, and that's when she started crying, and then she dozed off for a little bit and then woke back up." Malachi said the driver initially offered to take them home but fled the scene when others approached. "But then when he saw the other people coming and looked at Serenity, he just drove off fast," Malachi said. Police confirmed that Serenity sustained a fractured femur in the crash and are continuing their investigation. "We have now an individual out in our community that has not been held accountable for this as of yet," police said. Authorities believe the driver is a man between the ages of 20 and 30 years old, driving an early 2000s gold Mercedes-Benz that may have damage to the driver’s side. "I can tell you that the police department is actively working this case. We have different disciplines within the police department looking into this to ensure that we get this person and hold this person accountable for what actually occurred that day," police said. Anyone with information is urged to contact Fort Pierce detectives. lead_independence.headline: Search warrant executed at Fort Pierce home tied to $7 million Southern Truss fraud case
lead_independence.lead: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office deputies executed a search warrant Tuesday morning at the Fort Pierce home of Laura Beth Grasso in the Indian River Estates neighborhood near Sunset Boulevard. Crime scene investigators were seen outside the home as part of the ongoing investigation into the Southern Truss fraud case. Grasso was arrested July 16 along with Sheri Lynn Harrs and Tina Marie Mejia following what the sheriff's office described as a years-long scheme targeting Southern Truss Companies. Grasso has pleaded not guilty to the charges.

lead_independence.headline: Father arrested in Virginia in connection with Fort Pierce infant malnutrition death
lead_independence.lead: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office announced Tuesday that Jason Gunter, 45, was taken into custody by the United States Marshals Service at his home in Mechanicsville, Virginia. Detectives had obtained an arrest warrant for Gunter in connection with the death of his 3-month-old son. He has been charged with felony child neglect causing great harm and is awaiting extradition to St. Lucie County.

hero.headline: Flood Advisory issued for western Martin County through 7:30 p.m. Thursday
hero.body:
A Flood Advisory remains in effect until 7:30 p.m. Thursday for western Martin County. Radar estimates indicate anywhere from 1 to 3 inches of rain have already fallen across the area.

An additional 1 to 2 inches of rainfall is expected before the advisory expires. The National Weather Service issued the alert as heavy rain continues to move through the western portion of the county.

A Flood Advisory means that flooding is occurring or is imminent in low-lying and poor drainage areas. Motorists should avoid driving through standing water and should be prepared for potential road closures.

Residents in western Martin County should monitor weather conditions and be alert for rapidly rising water in streams, creeks, and roadways. The advisory was issued early Thursday morning and covers areas away from the coastal communities.

cards.headline: Martin County sheriff warns of counterfeit Pokémon card sales after $1,200 in losses
cards.teaser: Two Martin County residents lost more than $1,200 after purchasing counterfeit Pokémon trading cards in recent weeks, according to the sheriff's office.
cards.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office is warning collectors to watch for counterfeit Pokémon trading cards after two local residents reported losing more than $1,200 in recent purchases. The reports were filed within the past few weeks. In both cases, the buyers believed they were purchasing authentic Pokémon cards but later learned the cards were not legitimate.

Rare cards can sell for hundreds or even thousands of dollars, making them a target for counterfeiters and online scammers. Fraudulent cards may be offered through online marketplaces, social media pages, and other sales platforms. The sheriff's office cautioned buyers not to assume an item is authentic simply because it appears legitimate or is listed on a well-known website.

Before making a purchase, buyers should research the card's typical value and investigate the seller's reputation. For expensive cards, authorities recommend having the item examined by a reputable trading card expert or professional authentication service before payment is made. Residents conducting in-person transactions may use the designated exchange parking spaces at the Martin County Sheriff's Office, which are monitored by cameras 24 hours a day.
cards.article_text: The Martin County Sheriff’s Office is warning collectors to watch for counterfeit Pokémon trading cards after two local residents reported losing more than $1,200 in recent purchases. The reports were filed within the past few weeks, according to the sheriff’s office. In both cases, the buyers believed they were purchasing authentic Pokémon cards but later learned the cards were not legitimate. Although Pokémon cards are often viewed as children’s collectibles, rare cards can sell for hundreds or even thousands of dollars. Their potential value has made them a target for counterfeiters and online scammers, authorities said. Fraudulent cards may be offered through online marketplaces, social media pages and other sales platforms. The sheriff’s office cautioned buyers not to assume an item is authentic simply because it appears legitimate or is listed on a well-known website. Before making a purchase, buyers should research the card’s typical value and investigate the seller’s reputation. Deals priced far below market value should be treated with caution. For expensive cards, authorities recommend having the item examined by a reputable trading-card expert or professional authentication service before payment is made. Buyers meeting sellers in person should also take time to inspect the cards carefully. See also: Police release photo of toy kitchen involved in Boynton toddler's death; family IDs girl The sheriff’s office noted that recovering money can be difficult once a transaction is complete, particularly when the item is later found to be counterfeit. Residents conducting in-person transactions may also use the designated exchange parking spaces at the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. The spaces are monitored by cameras 24 hours a day.

cards.headline: North Carolina family chased off road near I-95 in Martin County describes attack
cards.teaser: A North Carolina family visiting Florida with their young son was forced off the road near Kanner Highway, just west of I-95 in Martin County over the weekend.
cards.body:
Body camera footage shows a North Carolina couple and their young son walking out of the bushes and explaining to a Martin County sheriff's deputy what happened after being chased off the road near Kanner Highway, just west of I-95, over the weekend. The family appeared visibly shaken as they recounted the incident.

The couple said the suspect chased the man's sister for miles, prompting the wife to call 911. The man explained that he and his wife tried to intervene, but the driver then turned his focus on them. After pulling over, the man said the driver came back. The driver continued to follow the couple, eventually forcing them off the road. The man's sister managed to escape.

The driver, identified as Michael Spires, was taken into custody at a nearby gas station. Sheriff John Budensiek said the family did not know what was coming next and were extremely grateful that they did not get injured. Budensiek added that the suspect did not have a gun and that it could have ended much worse.
cards.article_text: Body camera footage shows a North Carolina family walking out of the bushes and explaining what happened after being chased off the road near Kanner Highway, just west of I-95 in Martin County over the weekend. The couple, visiting Florida with their young son, appeared visibly shaken as they recounted the incident to a sheriff's deputy, explaining what happened to them and the man's sister, who was driving ahead of them. "He was trying to run her off the road," the man said, referring to his sister. Were you guys traveling together? Okay," the deputy responded. The family said the suspect, seen in the body camera footage, chased the man's sister for miles, prompting his wife to call 911. "The lady that he's chasing, she has a little baby in her car," the wife said. "He's literally chasing her with his lasers on. She's trying to get away from him. She said he's pressing brakes, trying to get away, and he said he's chasing her." The man explained that he and his wife tried to intervene, but the unknown driver then turned his focus on them. "You all pulled over?" the deputy asked. "Yeah, we all pulled over essentially because he stopped us again. So, I figured if we let him go far enough ahead, maybe we'll keep going. He got out, and he came back," the man said. The man's sister managed to escape, but the driver continued to follow him and his wife, eventually forcing them off the road. "And he's chasing you in the car?" the deputy asked. He evasive maneuver just off the road. He pit you," the man said. The driver, identified as Michael Spires, was taken into custody at a nearby gas station. "They did not know what was coming next, so they are extremely grateful that they didn't get injured and that it wasn't worse," Sheriff John Budensiek said. "Thank goodness our suspect didn't have a gun. It could have ended so much worse."
